text:
maria: Heads-up — we need a concrete plan for tenant rollforward snapshotting + pin pruning. Saw a spike in evictions yesterday when a few tenants updated model pins at once.
jyoti: Can you share the eviction trace? is it the resolver churning or eviction controller lagging?
maria: resolver churn + cascade: client probes hit old pinned versions causing retries which then created lots of ephemeral allocations. ops traced it to the pin-prune job running as a sweep.
sam: +1 we should avoid global sweeps during rollouts. Proposal: per-tenant incremental snapshot + graceful prune window.
kevin: sketch: when a tenant updates pin -> create a rollforward snapshot object with target_version, prev_version, timestamp, and a prune_deadline = now + grace_window. prune job operates only on snapshots with expired prune_deadline.
lia: sounds safer. what should grace_window be? we don't want to keep old models forever either.
maria: initial suggestion 2h for normal tenants, 24h for enterprise tenants behind dedicated pools. We also need a fast-fallback path if capacity is constrained.
jyoti: ops consideration: during the grace_window we should still accept requests routed to prev_version (to avoid 5xx), but mark traffic as draining. That implies we need per-allocation draining metadata and a health state.
sam: we can encode draining metadata on the snapshot and on allocations: allocation.metadata = {"draining": "true", "snapshot_id": "s-abc123"}. prune job checks allocations tag before evicting.
kevin: pseudoconfig idea:
```
rollforward_snapshotting: 
  grace_window_default: 2h
  enterprise_grace_window: 24h
  prune_batch_size: 100
  snapshot_retention_tag: "snapshot_id"
```
lia: +1 to config. also add telemetry: counter for "pin_prune_attempts", gauge for "active_snapshots", and histogram for "time_to_prune" so we can tune.
ops-bot: alert: evo-controller detected 120 evictions in 5m for tenant=tidepool — correlating with pin-update events.
maria: good, telemetry will help. one more thing: API surface — clients that do pinned reads should be able to request "pinning: prefer_latest" or "pinning: strict". prefer_latest allows routing to new version but accept old until prune. strict refuses until pin finalized.
jyoti: agree. Also need rollout metadata exposed in the model catalog: snapshot_id, origin_user, started_at, prune_deadline, fallback_order.
sam: rollout metadata shape suggestion: {"snapshot_id": "s-...", "versions": ["v2","v3"], "started_at": "2026-03-01T12:00:00Z", "prune_deadline": "2026-03-01T14:00:00Z", "tier": "enterprise"} (store as compact protobuf on control plane).
kevin: small operational note — make prune jobs idempotent and rate-limited. use leader election per-tenant to avoid thundering herds.
lia: do we need a migration path for existing pins? how do we backfill snapshots?
maria: backfill plan: generate snapshot for any pin-change in the last 48h; mark prune_deadline based on tenant tier and current time. run backfill during low-traffic windows.
jyoti: ok next steps: write up RFC with data model + config + telemetry + API flags. sam/kevin to draft control-plane impl, lia to draft ops runbook, jyoti to draft client semantics. i'll collect and schedule a 30m sync. :calendar: :+1:
